31691671 ModuleSpeci2
31691691 The specification for a module, used for loading.
31691742 A module's spec is the source for information about the module.  For
31691811 data associated with the module, including source, use the spec's
31691877 loader.
31691886 `name` is the absolute name of the module.  `loader` is the loader
31691953 to use when loading the module.  `parent` is the name of the
31692014 package the module is in.  The parent is derived from the name.
31692079 `is_package` determines if the module is considered a package or
31692144 not.  On modules this is reflected by the `__path__` attribute.
31692209 `origin` is the specific location used by the loader from which to
31692276 load the module, if that information is available.  When filename is
31692345 set, origin will match.
31692370 `has_location` indicates that a spec's "origin" reflects a location.
31692439 When this is True, `__file__` attribute of the module is set.
31692502 `cached` is the location of the cached bytecode file, if any.  It
31692568 corresponds to the `__cached__` attribute.
31692612 `submodule_search_locations` is the sequence of path entries to
31692676 search when importing submodules.  If set, is_package should be
31692740 True--and False otherwise.
31692768 Packages are simply modules that (may) have submodules.  If a spec
31692835 has a non-None value in `submodule_search_locations`, the import
31692900 system will consider modules loaded from the spec as packages.
31692964 Only finders (see importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder and
31693015 importlib.abc.PathEntryFinder) should modify ModuleSpec instances.

31733509 \prog
31733626 OS routines for NT or Posix depending on what system we're on.
31733690 This exports:
31733704   - all functions from posix or nt, e.g. unlink, stat, etc.
31733764   - os.path is either posixpath or ntpath
31733806   - os.name is either 'posix' or 'nt'
31733844   - os.curdir is a string representing the current directory (always '.')
31733918   - os.pardir is a string representing the parent directory (always '..')
31733992   - os.sep is the (or a most common) pathname separator ('/' or '\\')
31734062   - os.extsep is the extension separator (always '.')
31734116   - os.altsep is the alternate pathname separator (None or '/')
31734180   - os.pathsep is the component separator used in $PATH etc
31734240   - os.linesep is the line separator in text files ('\n' or '\r\n')
31734308   - os.defpath is the default search path for executables
31734366   - os.devnull is the file path of the null device ('/dev/null', etc.)
31734438 Programs that import and use 'os' stand a better chance of being
31734503 portable between different platforms.  Of course, they must then
31734568 only use functions that are defined by all platforms (e.g., unlink
31734635 and opendir), and leave all pathname manipulation to os.path
31734696 (e.g., split and join).

31739704 renamesr
31741277 Directory tree generator.
31741304 For each directory in the directory tree rooted at top (including top
31741374 itself, but excluding '.' and '..'), yields a 3-tuple
31741429     dirpath, dirnames, filenames
31741463 dirpath is a string, the path to the directory.  dirnames is a list of
31741534 the names of the subdirectories in dirpath (including symlinks to directories,
31741613 and excluding '.' and '..').
31741642 filenames is a list of the names of the non-directory files in dirpath.
31741714 Note that the names in the lists are just names, with no path components.
31741788 To get a full path (which begins with top) to a file or directory in
31741857 dirpath, do os.path.join(dirpath, name).
31741899 If optional arg 'topdown' is true or not specified, the triple for a
31741968 directory is generated before the triples for any of its subdirectories
31742040 (directories are generated top down).  If topdown is false, the triple
31742111 for a directory is generated after the triples for all of its
31742173 subdirectories (directories are generated bottom up).
31742228 When topdown is true, the caller can modify the dirnames list in-place
31742299 (e.g., via del or slice assignment), and walk will only recurse into the
31742372 subdirectories whose names remain in dirnames; this can be used to prune the
31742449 search, or to impose a specific order of visiting.  Modifying dirnames when
31742525 topdown is false has no effect on the behavior of os.walk(), since the
31742596 directories in dirnames have already been generated by the time dirnames
31742669 itself is generated. No matter the value of topdown, the list of
31742734 subdirectories is retrieved before the tuples for the directory and its
31742806 subdirectories are generated.
31742837 By default errors from the os.scandir() call are ignored.  If
31742899 optional arg 'onerror' is specified, it should be a function; it
31742964 will be called with one argument, an OSError instance.  It can
31743027 report the error to continue with the walk, or raise the exception
31743094 to abort the walk.  Note that the filename is available as the
31743157 filename attribute of the exception object.
31743202 By default, os.walk does not follow symbolic links to subdirectories on
31743274 systems that support them.  In order to get this functionality, set the
31743346 optional argument 'followlinks' to true.
31743388 Caution:  if you pass a relative pathname for top, don't change the
31743456 current working directory between resumptions of walk.  walk never
31743523 changes the current directory, and assumes that the client doesn't
31743590 either.
31743599 Example:
31743609 import os
31743619 from os.path import join, getsize
31743653 for root, dirs, files in os.walk('python/Lib/xml'):
31743705     print(root, "consumes ")
31743734     print(sum(getsize(join(root, name)) for name in files), end=" ")
31743803     print("bytes in", len(files), "non-directory files")
31743860     if '__pycache__' in dirs:
31743890         dirs.remove('__pycache__')  # don't visit __pycache__ directories

31745223 dir_fdc
31745718 Directory tree generator.
31745745 This behaves exactly like walk(), except that it yields a 4-tuple
31745812     dirpath, dirnames, filenames, dirfd
31745853 `dirpath`, `dirnames` and `filenames` are identical to walk() output,
31745923 and `dirfd` is a file descriptor referring to the directory `dirpath`.
31745995 The advantage of fwalk() over walk() is that it's safe against symlink
31746066 races (when follow_symlinks is False).
31746106 If dir_fd is not None, it should be a file descriptor open to a directory,
31746181   and top should be relative; top will then be relative to that directory.
31746256   (dir_fd is always supported for fwalk.)
31746299 Caution:
31746308 Since fwalk() yields file descriptors, those are only valid until the
31746378 next iteration step, so you should dup() them if you want to keep them
31746449 for a longer period.
31746471 Example:
31746481 import os
31746491 for root, dirs, files, rootfd in os.fwalk('python/Lib/xml'):
31746552     print(root, "consumes", end="")
31746588     print(sum(os.stat(name, dir_fd=rootfd).st_size for name in files),
31746659           end="")
31746677     print("bytes in", len(files), "non-directory files")
31746734     if '__pycache__' in dirs:
31746764         dirs.remove('__pycache__')  # don't visit __pycache__ directories

31800889 Return the spec for the specified module.
31800932 First, sys.modules is checked to see if the module was already imported. If
31801008 so, then sys.modules[name].__spec__ is returned. If that happens to be
31801079 set to None, then ValueError is raised. If the module is not in
31801143 sys.modules, then sys.meta_path is searched for a suitable spec with the
31801216 value of 'path' given to the finders. None is returned if no spec could
31801288 be found.
31801299 Dotted names do not have their parent packages implicitly imported. You will
31801376 most likely need to explicitly import all parent packages in the proper
31801448 order for a submodule to get the correct spec.

31803762 A context manager that can temporarily skip the compatibility check.
31803832 NOTE: This function is meant to accommodate an unusual case; one
31803897 which is likely to eventually go away.  There's is a pretty good
31803962 chance this is not what you were looking for.
31804009 WARNING: Using this function to disable the check can lead to
31804071 unexpected behavior and even crashes.  It should only be used during
31804140 extension module development.
31804171 If "disable_check" is True then the compatibility check will not
31804236 happen while the context manager is active.  Otherwise the check
31804301 *will* happen.
31804317 Normally, extensions that do not support multiple interpreters
31804380 may not be imported in a subinterpreter.  That implies modules
31804443 that do not implement multi-phase init or that explicitly of out.
31804510 Likewise for modules import in a subinterpreter with its own GIL
31804575 when the extension does not support a per-interpreter GIL.  This
31804640 implies the module does not have a Py_mod_multiple_interpreters slot
31804709 set to Py_MOD_PER_INTERPRETER_GIL_SUPPORTED.
31804755 In both cases, this context manager may be used to temporarily
31804818 disable the check for compatible extension modules.
31804871 You can get the same effect as this function by implementing the
31804936 basic interface of multi-phase init (PEP 489) and lying about
31804998 support for multiple interpreters (or per-interpreter GIL).

31824413 Returns a 2-tuple (drive_or_unc, path); either part may be empty.

31849393 Defines the interface for stateless encoders/decoders.
31849449 The .encode()/.decode() methods may use different error
31849505 handling schemes by providing the errors argument. These
31849562 string values are predefined:
31849593  'strict' - raise a ValueError error (or a subclass)
31849646  'ignore' - ignore the character and continue with the next
31849706  'replace' - replace with a suitable replacement character;
31849766             Python will use the official U+FFFD REPLACEMENT
31849826             CHARACTER for the builtin Unicode codecs on
31849882             decoding and '?' on encoding.
31849924  'surrogateescape' - replace with private code points U+DCnn.
31849986  'xmlcharrefreplace' - Replace with the appropriate XML
31850042                        character reference (only for encoding).
31850106  'backslashreplace'  - Replace with backslashed escape sequences.
31850172  'namereplace'       - Replace with \N{...} escape sequences
31850233                        (only for encoding).
31850278 The set of allowed values can be extended via register_error.
31850388 Encodes the object input and returns a tuple (output
31850441 object, length consumed).
31850468 errors defines the error handling to apply. It defaults to
31850527 'strict' handling.
31850547 The method may not store state in the Codec instance. Use
31850605 StreamWriter for codecs which have to keep state in order to
31850666 make encoding efficient.
31850692 The encoder must be able to handle zero length input and
31850749 return an empty object of the output object type in this
31850806 situation.

31863915 resulting object.
31863934 chars indicates the number of decoded code points or bytes to
31863996 return. read() will never return more data than requested,
31864055 but it might return less, if there is not enough available.
31864116 size indicates the approximate maximum number of decoded
31864173 bytes or code points to read for decoding. The decoder
31864228 can modify this setting as appropriate. The default value
31864286 -1 indicates to read and decode as much as possible.  size
31864345 is intended to prevent having to decode huge files in one

31864465 after the first line terminator in the input only the first line

31864674 it should read as much data as is allowed within the

31873685 encodingrd
31874094 StreamRecoder instances translate data from one encoding to another.
31874164 They use the complete set of APIs returned by the
31874214 codecs.lookup() function to implement their task.
31874265 Data written to the StreamRecoder is first decoded into an
31874324 intermediate format (depending on the "decode" codec) and then
31874387 written to the underlying stream using an instance of the provided
31874454 Writer class.
31874469 In the other direction, data is read from the underlying stream using
31874539 a Reader instance and then encoded and returned to the caller.
31874745 Creates a StreamRecoder instance which implements a two-way
31874805 conversion: encode and decode work on the frontend (the
31874861 data visible to .read() and .write()) while Reader and Writer
31874923 work on the backend (the data in stream).
31874966 You can use these objects to do transparent
31875010 transcodings from e.g. latin-1 to utf-8 and back.
31875061 stream must be a file-like object.
31875097 encode and decode must adhere to the Codec interface; Reader and
31875162 Writer must be factory functions or classes providing the
31875220 StreamReader and StreamWriter interfaces resp.
31875268 Error handling is done in the same way as defined for the
31875326 StreamWriter/Readers.

31879292 Note: The wrapped version will only accept the object format
31879353 defined by the codecs, i.e. Unicode objects for most builtin
31879414 codecs. Output is also codec dependent and will usually be
31879473 Unicode as well.
31879491 If encoding is not None, then the
31879525 underlying encoded files are always opened in binary mode.
31879584 The default file mode is 'r', meaning to open the file in read mode.

31879994 be used.

31887458 The io module provides the Python interfaces to stream handling. The
31887527 builtin open function is defined in this module.
31887577 At the top of the I/O hierarchy is the abstract base class IOBase. It
31887647 defines the basic interface to a stream. Note, however, that there is no
31887720 separation between reading and writing to streams; implementations are
31887791 allowed to raise an OSError if they do not support a given operation.
31887862 Extending IOBase is RawIOBase which deals simply with the reading and
31887932 writing of raw bytes to a stream. FileIO subclasses RawIOBase to provide
31888005 an interface to OS files.
31888032 BufferedIOBase deals with buffering on a raw byte stream (RawIOBase). Its
31888106 subclasses, BufferedWriter, BufferedReader, and BufferedRWPair buffer
31888176 streams that are readable, writable, and both respectively.
31888236 BufferedRandom provides a buffered interface to random access
31888298 streams. BytesIO is a simple stream of in-memory bytes.
31888355 Another IOBase subclass, TextIOBase, deals with the encoding and decoding
31888429 of streams into text. TextIOWrapper, which extends it, is a buffered text
31888503 interface to a buffered raw stream (`BufferedIOBase`). Finally, StringIO
31888576 is an in-memory stream for text.
31888610 Argument names are not part of the specification, and only the arguments
31888683 of open() are intended to be used as keyword arguments.
31888740 data:
31888747 DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE
31888768    An int containing the default buffer size used by the module's buffered
31888843    I/O classes. open() uses the file's blksize (as obtained by os.stat) if
31888918    possible.

32050849 A decorator indicating abstract methods.
32050891 Requires that the metaclass is ABCMeta or derived from it.  A
32050953 class that has a metaclass derived from ABCMeta cannot be
32051011 instantiated unless all of its abstract methods are overridden.
32051075 The abstract methods can be called using any of the normal
32051134 'super' call mechanisms.  abstractmethod() may be used to declare
32051200 abstract methods for properties and descriptors.
32051250 Usage:
32051258     class C(metaclass=ABCMeta):
32051290         @abstractmethod
32051314         def my_abstract_method(self, arg1, arg2, argN):
32051370             ...

32053443 ABCMeta
32053460 Metaclass for defining Abstract Base Classes (ABCs).
32053514 Use this metaclass to create an ABC.  An ABC can be subclassed
32053577 directly, and then acts as a mix-in class.  You can also register
32053643 unrelated concrete classes (even built-in classes) and unrelated
32053708 ABCs as 'virtual subclasses' -- these and their descendants will
32053773 be considered subclasses of the registering ABC by the built-in
32053837 issubclass() function, but the registering ABC won't show up in
32053901 their MRO (Method Resolution Order) nor will method
32053953 implementations defined by the registering ABC be callable (not
32054017 even via super()).

32059713 r*\+S
32059752 Append module search paths for third-party packages to sys.path.
32059818 ****************************************************************
32059883 * This module is automatically imported during initialization. *
32059948 ****************************************************************
32060014 This will append site-specific paths to the module search path.  On
32060082 Unix (including Mac OSX), it starts with sys.prefix and
32060138 sys.exec_prefix (if different) and appends
32060181 lib/python<version>/site-packages.
32060216 On other platforms (such as Windows), it tries each of the
32060275 prefixes directly, as well as with lib/site-packages appended.  The
32060343 resulting directories, if they exist, are appended to sys.path, and
32060411 also inspected for path configuration files.
32060457 If a file named "pyvenv.cfg" exists one directory above sys.executable,
32060529 sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix are set to that directory and
32060590 it is also checked for site-packages (sys.base_prefix and
32060648 sys.base_exec_prefix will always be the "real" prefixes of the Python
32060718 installation). If "pyvenv.cfg" (a bootstrap configuration file) contains
32060791 the key "include-system-site-packages" set to anything other than "false"
32060865 (case-insensitive), the system-level prefixes will still also be
32060930 searched for site-packages; otherwise they won't.
32060981 All of the resulting site-specific directories, if they exist, are
32061048 appended to sys.path, and also inspected for path configuration
32061112 files.
32061120 A path configuration file is a file whose name has the form
32061180 <package>.pth; its contents are additional directories (one per line)
32061250 to be added to sys.path.  Non-existing directories (or
32061305 non-directories) are never added to sys.path; no directory is added to
32061376 sys.path more than once.  Blank lines and lines beginning with
32061439 '#' are skipped. Lines starting with 'import' are executed.
32061500 For example, suppose sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix are set to
32061563 /usr/local and there is a directory /usr/local/lib/python2.5/site-packages
32061638 with three subdirectories, foo, bar and spam, and two path
32061697 configuration files, foo.pth and bar.pth.  Assume foo.pth contains the
32061768 following:
32061780   # foo package configuration
32061810   foo
32061816   bar
32061822   bletch
32061832 and bar.pth contains:
32061855   # bar package configuration
32061885   bar
32061892 Then the following directories are added to sys.path, in this order:
32061962   /usr/local/lib/python2.5/site-packages/bar
32062007   /usr/local/lib/python2.5/site-packages/foo
32062053 Note that bletch is omitted because it doesn't exist; bar precedes foo
32062124 because bar.pth comes alphabetically before foo.pth; and spam is
32062189 omitted because it is not mentioned in either path configuration file.
32062261 The readline module is also automatically configured to enable
32062324 completion for systems that support it.  This can be overridden in
32062391 sitecustomize, usercustomize or PYTHONSTARTUP.  Starting Python in
32062458 isolated mode (-I) disables automatic readline configuration.
32062521 After these operations, an attempt is made to import a module
32062583 named sitecustomize, which can perform arbitrary additional
32062643 site-specific customizations.  If this import fails with an
32062703 ImportError exception, it is silently ignored.

32096205 dump($module, value, file, version=version, /, *, allow_code=True)
32096276 Write the value on the open file.
32096311   value
32096319     Must be a supported type.
32096349   file
32096356     Must be a writeable binary file.
32096393   version
32096403     Indicates the data format that dump should use.
32096455   allow_code
32096468     Allow to write code objects.
32096502 If the value has (or contains an object that has) an unsupported type, a
32096575 ValueError exception is raised - but garbage data will also be written
32096646 to the file. The object will not be properly read back by load().
32096717 This module contains functions that can read and write Python values in
32096789 a binary format. The format is specific to Python, but independent of
32096859 machine architecture issues.
32096889 Not all Python object types are supported; in general, only objects
32096957 whose value is independent from a particular invocation of Python can be
32097030 written and read by this module. The following types are supported:
32097098 None, integers, floating-point numbers, strings, bytes, bytearrays,
32097166 tuples, lists, sets, dictionaries, and code objects, where it
32097228 should be understood that tuples, lists and dictionaries are only
32097294 supported as long as the values contained therein are themselves
32097359 supported; and recursive lists and dictionaries should not be written
32097429 (they will cause infinite loops).
32097464 Variables:
32097476 version -- indicates the format that the module uses. Version 0 is the
32097547     historical format, version 1 shares interned strings and version 2
32097618     uses a binary format for floating-point numbers.
32097671     Version 3 shares common object references (New in version 3.4).
32097740 Functions:
32097752 dump() -- write value to a file
32097784 load() -- read value from a file
32097817 dumps() -- marshal value as a bytes object
32097860 loads() -- read value from a bytes-like object
32097917 load($module, file, /, *, allow_code=True)
32097964 Read one value from the open file and return it.
32098014   file
32098021     Must be readable binary file.
32098055   allow_code
32098068     Allow to load code objects.
32098101 If no valid value is read (e.g. because the data has a different Python
32098173 version's incompatible marshal format), raise EOFError, ValueError or
32098243 TypeError.
32098255 Note: If an object containing an unsupported type was marshalled with
32098325 dump(), load() will substitute None for the unmarshallable type.

32098489   allow_code

32194749 Windows: mmap(fileno, length[, tagname[, access[, offset]]])
32194811 Maps length bytes from the file specified by the file handle fileno,
32194880 and returns a mmap object.  If length is larger than the current size
32194950 of the file, the file is extended to contain length bytes.  If length
32195020 is 0, the maximum length of the map is the current size of the file,
32195089 except that if the file is empty Windows raises an exception (you cannot
32195162 create an empty mapping on Windows).
32195200 Unix: mmap(fileno, length[, flags[, prot[, access[, offset[, trackfd]]]]])
32195276 Maps length bytes from the file specified by the file descriptor fileno,
32195349 and returns a mmap object.  If length is 0, the maximum length of the map
32195423 will be the current size of the file when mmap is called.
32195481 flags specifies the nature of the mapping. MAP_PRIVATE creates a
32195546 private copy-on-write mapping, so changes to the contents of the mmap
32195616 object will be private to this process, and MAP_SHARED creates a mapping
32195689 that's shared with all other processes mapping the same areas of the file.
32195764 The default value is MAP_SHARED.
32195798 To map anonymous memory, pass -1 as the fileno (both versions).

32197709 channel_close(cid, *, send=None, recv=None, force=False)
32197767 Close the channel for all interpreters.
32197808 If the channel is empty then the keyword args are ignored and both
32197875 ends are immediately closed.  Otherwise, if 'force' is True then
32197940 all queued items are released and both ends are immediately
32198000 closed.
32198009 If the channel is not empty *and* 'force' is False then following
32198075 happens:
32198085  * recv is True (regardless of send):
32198123    - raise ChannelNotEmptyError
32198155  * recv is None and send is None:
32198189    - raise ChannelNotEmptyError
32198221  * send is True and recv is not True:
32198259    - fully close the 'send' end
32198291    - close the 'recv' end to interpreters not already receiving
32198355    - fully close it once empty
32198387 Closing an already closed channel results in a ChannelClosedError.
32198455 Once the channel's ID has no more ref counts in any interpreter
32198519 the channel will be destroyed.

33452859 select
33452875 This module supports asynchronous I/O on multiple file descriptors.
33452944 *** IMPORTANT NOTICE ***
33452969 On Windows, only sockets are supported; on Unix, all file descriptors.
33453051 select($module, rlist, wlist, xlist, timeout=None, /)
33453109 Wait until one or more file descriptors are ready for some kind of I/O.
33453182 The first three arguments are iterables of file descriptors to be waited
33453260 rlist -- wait until ready for reading
33453298 wlist -- wait until ready for writing
33453336 xlist -- wait for an "exceptional condition"
33453381 If only one kind of condition is required, pass [] for the other lists.
33453454 A file descriptor is either a socket or file object, or a small integer
33453526 gotten from a fileno() method call on one of those.
33453579 The optional 4th argument specifies a timeout in seconds; it may be
33453647 a floating-point number to specify fractions of seconds.  If it is absent
33453721 or None, the call will never time out.
33453761 The return value is a tuple of three lists corresponding to the first
33453831 three arguments; each contains the subset of the corresponding file
33453899 descriptors that are ready.
33453928 *** IMPORTANT NOTICE ***
33453953 On Windows, only sockets are supported; on Unix, all file
33454011 descriptors can be used.
33454171 arguments 1-3 must be sequences
33454203 too many file descriptors in select()
33454243 timeout must be a float or None
33454275 timeout must be non-negative
